content.stem: A pressure vessel shell had an original thickness of 0.5 in. A thickness reading 8 years later is 0.38 in. What is the long-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.015 in/yr
0.03 in/yr
0.12 in/yr
content.explanation: Long-term corrosion rate = (t_initial − t_actual) / time = (0.5 − 0.38) / 8 = 0.015 in/yr.

content.stem: A CML measured 0.42 in. at the previous inspection and 0.39 in. at the current inspection 5 years later. What is the short-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.03 in/yr
0.006 in/yr
0.003 in/yr
0.078 in/yr
content.explanation: Short-term corrosion rate = (t_previous − t_actual) / time = (0.42 − 0.39) / 5 = 0.006 in/yr.

content.stem: A vessel component measures t_actual = 0.360 in., with t_required = 0.150 in. and a corrosion rate of 0.012 in/yr. What is the remaining life?
options: 8.75 years
30 years
17.5 years
12.5 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required) / corrosion rate = (0.360 - 0.150) / 0.012 = 17.5 years.

content.stem: A component has an actual thickness of 0.445 in. and a required thickness of 0.3 in. What is the remaining corrosion allowance?
options: 0.3 in
content.explanation: Remaining corrosion allowance = t_actual − t_required = 0.445 − 0.3 = 0.145 in.

content.stem: The remaining life of a vessel is calculated to be 12 years. Per API 510, the internal/on-stream inspection interval shall not exceed which value (assuming this governs and no RBI assessment is used)?
options: 6 years
12 years
3 years
24 years
content.explanation: API 510 limits the internal or on-stream inspection interval to the lesser of one-half the remaining life or 10 years. One-half of 12 = 6 years, which is less than 10, so 6 years governs.

content.stem: A vessel's remaining life is 30 years. Without an RBI assessment, what is the maximum internal or on-stream inspection interval per API 510?
options: 15 years
10 years
30 years
7.5 years
content.explanation: The interval is the lesser of one-half remaining life (15 years) or 10 years. Ten years governs because it is less than 15.

content.stem: A shell measures 0.5 in. with a corrosion rate of 0.01 in/yr. For an MAWP assessment covering the next 10-year interval, what thickness should be used (deduct the corrosion expected before the next inspection)?
options: 0.3 in
0.5 in
0.4 in
content.explanation: t_used = t_measured − (corrosion rate × interval) = 0.5 − (0.01 × 10) = 0.4 in.

content.stem: A vessel part is located 35 ft below the liquid surface. Using the exam convention (specific gravity = 1.0), what is the static head pressure acting on that part?
options: 7.58 psi
35 psi
content.explanation: Static head = 0.433 psi/ft × height × SG = 0.433 × 35 × 1.0 = 15.15 psi.

content.stem: The MAWP at the top of a vertical vessel is 100 psi. A nozzle is 50 ft below the top. What total pressure (MAWP + static head, SG = 1.0) acts at the nozzle?
options: 1 psi
content.explanation: Total = MAWP + static head = 100 + (0.433 × 50) = 121.65 psi.

content.stem: Determine the required thickness of a cylindrical shell for internal pressure (circumferential stress). P = 300 psi, inside radius R = 30 in., S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PR/(SE − 0.6P).
A cylindrical shell has corroded thickness t = 0.5 in., inside radius R = 24 in., S = 17500 psi, and E = 0.85. What is the vessel-part MAWP (circumferential stress)? Use P = SEt/(R + 0.6t).

A cylindrical shell requires a pressure-design thickness from t = PR/(SE − 0.6P) with P = 250 psi, R = 30 in., S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. If a corrosion allowance of 0.125 in. must be added, what is the total required thickness?
Determine the required thickness of a hemispherical head: P = 400 psi, inside radius R = 30 in., S = 17500 psi, E = 1. Use t = PR/(2SE - 0.2P).
content.explanation: t = PR/(2SE - 0.2P) = (400 x 30) / ((2 x 17500 x 1) - 0.2 x 400) = 0.3436 in. Using the cylinder formula (0.6953 in) is the common error; a hemi-head needs roughly half the thickness of a cylinder of equal radius.

content.stem: Determine the required thickness of a 2:1 ellipsoidal head: P = 300 psi, inside diameter D = 60 in., S = 17500 psi, E = 1. Use t = PD/(2SE - 0.2P).
content.explanation: t = PD/(2SE - 0.2P) = (300 x 60) / ((2 x 17500 x 1) - 0.2 x 300) = 0.5152 in. Using radius instead of diameter (0.2576 in) is the classic error.

content.stem: A Type 1 (double-welded butt) longitudinal joint is fully radiographed. What joint efficiency E is used per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: For a Type 1 joint with full radiography, Table UW-12 gives E = 1.00. Spot RT would give 0.85 and no RT 0.70.

content.stem: A Type 1 butt-welded longitudinal seam was spot radiographed. What joint efficiency applies per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: A Type 1 joint with spot RT is assigned E = 0.85 in Table UW-12.

content.stem: A Type 2 single-welded butt joint with a backing strip left in place receives no radiography. What is the joint efficiency per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: A Type 2 joint (backing strip) with no RT is assigned E = 0.65 in Table UW-12.

content.stem: For a seamless cylindrical shell section (no longitudinal weld), what joint efficiency does API 510 / UW-12(d) permit when evaluating the circumferential-stress (longitudinal-joint) minimum thickness?
content.explanation: Per UW-12(d), seamless vessel sections and heads may be assigned E = 1.00 for the longitudinal joint when checking circumferential stress (the controlling case for thickness).

content.stem: A vessel has an MAWP of 200 psi. Assuming the test-temperature and design-temperature allowable stresses are equal, what is the standard hydrostatic test pressure per current ASME VIII-1 (UG-99(b))?
options: 300 psi
200 psi
260 psi
220 psi
content.explanation: Standard hydrostatic test pressure = 1.3 × MAWP × (S_test/S_design). With the stress ratio = 1, = 1.3 × 200 = 260 psi. (The 1.5× factor is the older pre-1999 basis.)

content.stem: A vessel has MAWP = 150 psi. The ratio of allowable stress at test temperature to that at design temperature is 1.2. What is the hydrostatic test pressure per UG-99(b)?
options: 195 psi
27 psi
18 psi
234 psi
content.explanation: Test pressure = 1.3 × MAWP × (S_test/S_design) = 1.3 × 150 × 1.2 = 234 psi.

content.stem: A fillet weld has a required throat dimension of 0.35 in. Using the exam conversion factor of 0.7, what is the corresponding leg dimension?
options: 0.5 in
0.2 in
0.3 in
0.7 in
content.explanation: Throat = 0.7 × leg, so leg = throat / 0.7 = 0.35 / 0.7 = 0.5 in.

content.stem: A fillet weld has a leg dimension of 0.5 in. Using the 0.7 conversion factor, what is the effective throat?
options: 0.5 in

content.stem: Per API 510, who has overall responsibility for the in-service inspection program, including compliance with the code?
options: The organization performing repairs
The jurisdiction having authority
The owner/user of the equipment
The authorized inspection agency
content.explanation: API 510 assigns overall responsibility for the inspection, repair, alteration, and rerating program to the owner/user.

content.stem: Under API 510, who is permitted to perform the actual inspection work and data collection under the direction of the API authorized inspector?
options: Only personnel employed by the jurisdiction
The process engineer assigned to the unit
Operations staff during normal rounds
Examiners working under the inspector
content.explanation: Examiners may perform NDE and collect data; they need not be certified API inspectors but work under the authorized inspector, who remains responsible for evaluation and acceptance.

content.stem: API 510 applies primarily to which equipment?
options: In-service vessels: inspection, rating, repair, alteration
New pressure vessels during original code construction
Atmospheric and low-pressure bulk storage tank shells
Buried and aboveground process piping circuit systems
content.explanation: API 510 covers in-service pressure vessels — inspection, rating, repair, and alteration. New construction is covered by the construction code (e.g., ASME VIII).

content.stem: When establishing the MAWP for an existing pressure vessel, which thickness should be used in the calculation?
options: The original nominal thickness from the U-1 data report
Actual thickness less corrosion before the next inspection
The minimum thickness value stamped on the nameplate
The as-fabricated thickness at the heaviest shell course
content.explanation: Rerating/MAWP determinations use the actual measured thickness minus the corrosion allowance that will be lost before the next inspection date.

content.stem: A vessel may be rerated to a different MAWP only when which condition is met?
options: Informal verbal approval is obtained from the owner/user
The vessel has been in service for more than ten years
Calculations to the construction code, fully documented
A pressure test is substituted for the rating calculation
content.explanation: Rerating requires calculations per the applicable construction code, documentation, and (typically) updating the nameplate; it is performed by or with the manufacturer/engineer per API 510.

content.stem: Condition monitoring locations (CMLs) are best described as:
options: Locations where pressure-relief devices are installed
Zones reserved exclusively for welded repair activity
Points established only for recording nameplate data
Designated areas monitored for damage and thickness
content.explanation: CMLs are designated areas on a vessel where inspections (often thickness readings) are taken to monitor the presence and rate of damage.

content.stem: For a vessel subject to localized corrosion, the selection and number of CMLs should be:
options: Increased in number and placed to detect the damage
Reduced to a single representative monitoring point
Replaced entirely by routine general visual checks
Fixed only at the bottom head and lowest shell course
content.explanation: Where localized corrosion is expected, more CMLs are used and placed to detect the specific damage mechanism rather than relying on a few general points.

content.stem: An external inspection of an in-service vessel can typically be performed:
options: Only when shut down, opened, and entered
While the vessel remains on-stream
Only during the hydrostatic pressure test
Only by a representative of the jurisdiction
content.explanation: External inspections are generally on-stream activities; internal inspections require the vessel to be shut down and opened.

content.stem: The external inspection interval for most pressure vessels is not to exceed:
options: Not to exceed one year under any circumstance
Fixed at ten years regardless of the service
Not to exceed five years (or next internal)
Set at twenty years for all external surfaces
content.explanation: API 510 generally limits external inspection intervals to 5 years (or the next internal/on-stream inspection, if sooner).

content.stem: When a risk-based inspection (RBI) assessment is used to set inspection intervals, API 510 requires that it be:
options: Performed only once and never revisited later
Limited strictly to external visual inspection
Reviewed and approved by the welder of record
Documented and updated at the set interval
content.explanation: RBI assessments must be documented and reassessed/updated periodically and when conditions change (per API 510 referencing API 580).

content.stem: Use of an RBI assessment in accordance with API 510 may allow the internal/on-stream inspection interval to:
options: Exceed the default limits when risk is justified
Be fixed at exactly ten years for all equipment
Be eliminated for the equipment item entirely
Be set solely at the discretion of the welder
content.explanation: A documented RBI assessment can justify intervals beyond the default limits, provided risk is managed and the assessment is maintained.

content.stem: Which of the following is, by definition, an ALTERATION rather than a repair?
options: Replacing a section with identical material
A change beyond the original design basis
Re-welding a cracked attachment weld
Touch-up of an external protective coating
content.explanation: An alteration changes the vessel from its original design (e.g., adding a nozzle, increasing MAWP). A repair restores the vessel to a safe operating condition without such a change.

content.stem: Welded repairs and alterations to pressure vessels must be authorized by, and performed to procedures acceptable to, the:
options: The operations shift supervisor on duty at the time
The contracted coating and insulation applicator crew
The authorized inspector, with engineering as needed
The equipment insurer or underwriting representative
content.explanation: API 510 requires the authorized inspector to authorize repair/alteration work (with engineering involvement for alterations and certain repairs), using qualified procedures.

content.stem: Permanent records for a pressure vessel should include which of the following?
options: Only the most recently completed inspection report
Operator shift rotation and meal break schedules
Only the raw ultrasonic thickness measurement data
Design data, inspection history, and repair records
content.explanation: Permanent records include design and construction documentation, inspection results and history, and records of repairs, alterations, and reratings.

content.stem: Integrity operating windows (IOWs) are used to:
options: Limits on process variables to protect integrity
A posted schedule governing operator rest breaks
A reference table defining the required weld sizes
The documented basis for setting the hydrotest pressure
content.explanation: IOWs define acceptable ranges for process variables (temperature, pressure, chemistry) that, if exceeded, could accelerate damage; they support inspection planning.

content.stem: API 510 directs special attention to corrosion under insulation (CUI) for carbon and low-alloy steel vessels operating in which approximate temperature range?
options: Only below minus 50 F
Roughly 10 F to 350 F
Only above 1000 F
Only exactly at ambient temperature
content.explanation: CUI is most aggressive where insulation traps moisture against the metal. For carbon/low-alloy steel the susceptible band is commonly cited as roughly 10 F to 350 F (per API RP 571 3.22, the in-scope reference for 510; API 583 gives the same carbon-steel band). Austenitic stainless has a separate external-chloride-SCC concern range. Confirm exact bounds against the RP 571 edition on the current effectivity sheet.

content.stem: When averaging thickness measurements across a corroded region to determine compliance, the measurements should be averaged over a length that is:
options: Across the entire overall length of the vessel shell
Over any arbitrary length the operator may select
Within code-defined averaging lengths for the method
At a single isolated thickness measurement point
content.explanation: Thickness averaging must follow the applicable code/assessment rules for averaging length; arbitrary averaging can mask localized thin areas.

content.stem: When a vessel is found with damage that is below minimum required thickness or contains a flaw, a fitness-for-service assessment per API 579 may be used to:
options: Automatically condemn and retire the affected vessel
Eliminate the need for any further future inspection
Raise the MAWP rating without any further calculation
Judge suitability for continued service at conditions
content.explanation: API 579 FFS provides quantitative methods to evaluate flaws/damage and decide on continued service, rerating, repair, or replacement.

content.stem: Per API RP 571, atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel is generally most severe in which environment?
options: Marine air with chlorides and wet/dry cycling
Hot, dry inland desert air with low humidity
Continuously submerged full-immersion service
Inert-gas blanketed and permanently sealed space
content.explanation: Chloride-laden marine air with wet/dry cycling produces the highest atmospheric corrosion rates on carbon steel.

content.stem: Caustic corrosion (caustic gouging) of carbon steel is associated with:
options: Accumulation of dry chloride salt on the steel
Concentration of caustic under heat or deposits
Prolonged exposure to atmospheric oxygen alone
High-temperature dry hydrogen gas environments
content.explanation: Caustic corrosion results from concentration of caustic, often beneath deposits or in high-heat-flux areas, causing localized gouging.

content.stem: Caustic stress corrosion cracking (caustic embrittlement) of carbon steel requires which combination?
options: Low temperature with no applied tensile stress
Sustained vacuum conditions inside the vessel
Tensile stress plus caustic above a threshold
Pure water contact at ambient temperature only
content.explanation: Caustic SCC needs tensile stress (residual or applied) and caustic above a temperature/concentration threshold; PWHT is a common mitigation.

content.stem: Corrosion under insulation (CUI) of carbon steel is driven primarily by:
options: Dry intact insulation in good surface condition
Sustained high process-side vacuum on the wall
An inert dry atmosphere surrounding the shell
Water trapped against metal beneath insulation
content.explanation: CUI occurs when water is trapped under insulation against the metal; it is aggravated by chlorides and the wet temperature range.

content.stem: Amine stress corrosion cracking in carbon steel is best mitigated by which action?
options: Post-weld heat treatment to relieve residual stress
Deliberately increasing the operating stress level
Eliminating the inspection program from the unit
Reducing the process stream pH to below two units
content.explanation: Amine SCC is a form of alkaline SCC; PWHT to relieve residual stress is a primary mitigation for carbon steel in amine service.

content.stem: Boiler water and steam condensate corrosion is commonly the result of:
options: High alloy content present in the base steel
Dissolved oxygen or off-spec water chemistry
Excessive post-weld heat treatment exposure
Continuous nitrogen blanketing of the system
content.explanation: Condensate corrosion is often caused by dissolved gases (O2, CO2 forming carbonic acid) and poor water treatment.

content.stem: Chloride stress corrosion cracking primarily affects which material?
options: Carbon steel components in dry ambient service
Gray cast iron components at low temperature
Austenitic stainless steels under tensile stress
Copper and its alloys exclusively in service
content.explanation: Cl-SCC characteristically attacks austenitic stainless steels under tensile stress with chlorides and temperature; carbon steel is not typically susceptible.

content.stem: Erosion-corrosion is best described as:
options: Purely mechanical wear with no chemical action
Cracking that occurs under sustained static load
High-temperature time-dependent creep deformation
Combined flow effects and corrosion removing films
content.explanation: Erosion-corrosion combines flow-induced removal of protective films with corrosion, giving locally high metal-loss rates (e.g., at elbows, downstream of restrictions).

content.stem: Hydrochloric (HCl) acid corrosion in refinery units is commonly associated with:
options: Crude unit overhead from chloride salt hydrolysis
Cryogenic nitrogen storage and transfer service
Dry hydrogen gas service at elevated temperature
Caustic injection points located downstream only
content.explanation: HCl corrosion is a classic crude-unit overhead concern, where chloride salts hydrolyze to form HCl and attack carbon steel as dew point is reached.

content.stem: Sulfidation (sulfidic corrosion) of carbon steel becomes a significant concern above approximately:
options: Below roughly 100 F in wet condensate service
Above roughly 450 to 500 F with sulfur present
Near 260 F in essentially any process stream
Only at temperatures below ambient conditions
content.explanation: Sulfidation of carbon and low-alloy steels generally initiates around 450–500°F and increases with temperature and sulfur content; silicon content influences carbon-steel rates.

content.stem: Brittle fracture risk is greatest under which combination?
options: High temperature combined with very low stress
Vacuum service at moderately elevated temperature
Low temperature, a flaw, and sufficient stress
Fully annealed material held steady near 300 F
content.explanation: Brittle fracture requires a combination of low toughness (often at low temperature), a flaw/defect, and tensile stress; it is a key concern during hydrotest at low metal temperatures.

content.stem: High-temperature H2/H2S (hydrogen + hydrogen sulfide) corrosion in hydroprocessing units is evaluated using which classic reference data set?
options: Nelson curves applied for HTHA susceptibility
Larson-Miller parameter for creep rupture life
Goodman diagram for the fatigue endurance limit
Couper-Gorman curves for H2/H2S corrosion rates
content.explanation: High-temperature H2/H2S corrosion rates are estimated using the modified Couper-Gorman curves; the Nelson curves are for HTHA (a different mechanism).

content.stem: High-temperature hydrogen attack (HTHA) of carbon and low-alloy steels is assessed using which reference, and is mitigated primarily by what?
options: API 941 Nelson curves; Cr-Mo alloying for resistance
Couper-Gorman curves; surface coating for resistance
UW-12 joint efficiency tables; PWHT for resistance
Goodman fatigue diagram; lower stress for resistance
content.explanation: HTHA susceptibility is screened with the API 941 Nelson curves; resistance is provided by Cr-Mo alloying appropriate to the hydrogen partial pressure and temperature.

content.stem: Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC) is characterized by:
options: Uniform general thinning at low ambient temperature
Localized grooving in high-velocity high-TAN crude
Cracking that develops under caustic SCC exposure
Hydrogen blistering forming at steel inclusions
content.explanation: NAC produces localized, sometimes sharp-edged grooving in high-velocity zones of high-TAN crude at elevated temperatures (~425–750°F); sulfur content and alloy (Mo) influence severity.

content.stem: Which of the following is a form of wet H2S damage that does NOT necessarily require applied stress to occur?
options: Sulfide stress cracking under an applied load
Stress-oriented HIC needing high tensile stress
Hydrogen blistering accumulating at inclusions
Chloride SCC of austenitic stainless grades
content.explanation: Hydrogen blistering and HIC result from hydrogen accumulation at inclusions/laminations and can occur without applied stress; SSC and SOHIC are stress-related forms.

content.stem: Per API RP 572, before entering a pressure vessel for internal inspection, the most important precaution is to:
options: Carry extra protective coating material to the site
Remove the unit nameplate before making any entry
Raise the operating pressure to perform the check
Establish safe confined-space entry conditions first
content.explanation: Confined-space entry preparation — isolation, depressurization, purging, gas testing, and permits — is the essential safety precaution before internal inspection.

content.stem: RP 572 identifies which method as the primary means of detecting general and localized internal metal loss in a vessel wall?
options: Ultrasonic thickness measurement of the wall
Visual examination of the outer surface only
Hardness testing of the vessel base material
Ferrite content measurement across the welds
content.explanation: Ultrasonic thickness measurement is the standard method for quantifying wall loss; visual examination supports detection but does not quantify remaining wall.

content.stem: When inspecting a vessel with internal linings or refractory, RP 572 recommends paying particular attention to:
options: Only the vessel nameplate and code stamping area
Areas where lining damage exposes base metal
The external paint film condition exclusively
The relief valve set-pressure identification tag
content.explanation: Lining/refractory breaches can locally expose base metal to aggressive process conditions, so damaged lining areas warrant focused inspection of the underlying metal.

content.stem: RP 572 notes that small-bore connections and nozzles are important to inspect because they:
options: They are known never to corrode while in service
They are not pressure-containing parts at all
They are prone to fatigue and easily overlooked
They always retain extra wall thickness margin
content.explanation: Small-bore connections are prone to vibration fatigue and localized corrosion and are frequently missed in CML planning.

content.stem: The primary purpose of a pressure-relief device per RP 576 is to:
options: Improve the overall process flow efficiency rate
Measure the volumetric flow through the relief line
Reduce corrosion of the internal valve parts
Protect equipment from pressure above safe limits
content.explanation: Relief devices protect against overpressure by relieving when pressure reaches the set point.

content.stem: A common cause of relief valve malfunction identified in RP 576 is:
options: Corrosion, fouling, or plugging of internals or inlet
Excessive cleanliness of the internal trim and seat
Bench testing performed far too frequently in service
Painted or coated identification nameplates on it
content.explanation: Corrosion, fouling, and plugging of internals or connected piping are leading causes of relief valve failure to operate correctly.

content.stem: RP 576 indicates that the test interval for pressure-relief valves should be based primarily on:
options: A fixed twenty-year cycle applied to all valves
Service experience and prior as-found condition
The external body color or paint of the valve
The vessel's external surface coating schedule
content.explanation: Relief valve test intervals are set from service history and prior as-found conditions; fouling-prone services need shorter intervals.

content.stem: In SMAW (shielded metal arc welding), the arc shielding is provided by:
options: Gas supplied from an external inert shielding bottle
A circulating water jacket around the weld pool
Decomposition of the electrode flux coating
A vacuum drawn over the molten weld puddle area
content.explanation: SMAW shielding comes from gases produced as the electrode's flux coating decomposes in the arc; no external gas is used.

content.stem: The heat-affected zone (HAZ) of a weld is the region that:
options: The fusion zone that melted and resolidified
The wholly unaffected parent base metal region
The flux coating remaining on the weld surface
Base metal changed by heat but not melted
content.explanation: The HAZ is base metal adjacent to the fusion zone that did not melt but whose microstructure (and properties) changed due to the thermal cycle.

content.stem: Preheating prior to welding carbon and low-alloy steels primarily helps to:
options: Slow the cooling rate and hydrogen cracking risk
Increase the weld-metal cooling rate markedly
Add new alloying elements into the weld pool
Remove the need for adding any filler metal
content.explanation: Preheat slows the cooling rate, lowering the risk of forming hard, crack-susceptible microstructures and aiding hydrogen diffusion out of the weld.

content.stem: Post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) of carbon steel weldments is performed mainly to:
options: Increase the residual stress within the joint
Relieve residual stress and temper the HAZ
Introduce more hydrogen into the weld metal
Deliberately cause distortion in the weldment
content.explanation: PWHT reduces residual stress and tempers hard microstructures, improving toughness and resistance to stress-corrosion mechanisms.

content.stem: Which weld discontinuity is generally considered the most detrimental because it is a sharp, planar, crack-like defect?
options: A uniform acceptable weld reinforcement profile
Slight undercut remaining within the code limits
A crack, being sharp, planar, and propagating
Acceptable scattered rounded weld metal porosity
content.explanation: Cracks are planar, sharp discontinuities that concentrate stress and propagate; they are the most serious type and are typically not acceptable.

content.stem: Positive material identification (PMI) per RP 578 is performed to:
options: Measure the component remaining wall thickness
Establish the relief device set pressure value
Detect surface-breaking cracking in the welds
Verify component alloy matches the specification
content.explanation: PMI verifies that installed materials have the specified alloy composition, guarding against material mix-ups that can cause in-service failures.

content.stem: The principal risk that a PMI program is designed to prevent is:
options: Installation of a wrong alloy that fails early
Application of an excess surface coating layer
Presence of extra unneeded wall thickness margin
Slow process flow through the installed component
content.explanation: A wrong alloy (e.g., carbon steel where a Cr-Mo or stainless was required) can corrode or fail rapidly; PMI catches such mix-ups.

content.stem: Per ASME Section VIII-1 (UW-3), a longitudinal (or any seam within a shell/head along the main axis) weld joint is classified as which category?
options: Category B
Category A
Category C
Category D
content.explanation: UW-3 Category A includes longitudinal welded joints in the main shell, and any welded joint within a head; Category B is circumferential, C is flange/tubesheet to shell, D is nozzle to shell/head.

content.stem: A circumferential weld joint connecting two cylindrical shell courses is which UW-3 category?
options: Category A
Category C
Category B
Category D
content.explanation: Circumferential joints in the main shell or connecting a head to the main shell are UW-3 Category B.

content.stem: The weld joint connecting a nozzle to the shell is classified as which category?
options: Category A
Category B
Category C
Category D
content.explanation: Nozzle-to-shell/head attachment welds are UW-3 Category D.

content.stem: The marking 'RT-1' on a vessel nameplate per UW-11 indicates that:
options: Full radiography per the RT-1 definition
No radiography performed on the vessel at all
Only spot radiography applied to the main seams
Only the two heads received full radiography
content.explanation: UW-11 marking RT-1 denotes full radiography of all Category A and B joints (and certain others) per the RT-1 definition. RT-2/3/4 denote lesser extents.

content.stem: A '2:1 ellipsoidal' head designation refers to the ratio of:
options: Wall thickness compared with the inside diameter
Major axis (diameter) to twice the depth
Overall length compared with the main weld size
Internal pressure compared with the allowable stress
content.explanation: A 2:1 ellipsoidal head is named for the 2:1 ratio of its major axis (the diameter D) to its minor axis (which equals twice the head depth, 2h). That ratio gives D = 4h, so the head depth h equals one-quarter of the diameter.

content.stem: During a hydrostatic test per UG-99, the inspection for leaks should be performed:
options: At the full peak hydrostatic test pressure value
Before the vessel has been pressurized at all
At not less than the test pressure divided by 1.3
Only after the vessel has been fully drained
content.explanation: UG-99 requires the visual examination for leakage to be made at a pressure not less than the test pressure divided by 1.3, protecting personnel from inspecting at the peak test pressure.

content.stem: Per UCS-66, the need for impact testing of carbon and low-alloy steels is evaluated using:
options: A single fixed temperature for all steels
Joint efficiency tables from UW-12
The Couper-Gorman corrosion curves
Toughness curves of thickness versus MDMT
content.explanation: UCS-66 assigns materials to curves A–D; the curve and governing thickness give the MDMT at which impact testing is/ is not required (with possible exemptions in UG-20(f)).

content.stem: Which condition is part of the UG-20(f) impact-test exemption for carbon steel vessels?
options: Defined P-number, thickness, and temperature limits
Any design metal temperature below minus 50 F set
Any base-metal thickness without any restriction
Only the austenitic stainless steel material grades
content.explanation: UG-20(f) provides exemption from impact testing when specific P-Number, thickness, and design-temperature limits (and other conditions) are met.

content.stem: When a vessel is constructed to a joint efficiency requiring full radiography, which Section VIII requirement governs the extent of RT?
options: The UG-99 hydrostatic pressure test rules
UW-11 with UW-51 and UW-52 acceptance
The UCS-56 post-weld heat treatment rules
The UW-3 weld joint category definitions
content.explanation: UW-11 establishes RT requirements; UW-51 (full RT) and UW-52 (spot RT) give acceptance criteria for the radiographs.

content.stem: In ASME Section IX, the document that records the actual values used and the test results that support a welding procedure is the:
options: The WPS welding procedure specification sheet
The WPQ welder performance qualification record
The PQR (procedure qualification record)
The radiographic examination final test report
content.explanation: The PQR (Procedure Qualification Record) records the as-welded variables and mechanical test results that qualify the WPS.

content.stem: The Welder Performance Qualification (WPQ) demonstrates that:
options: The procedure itself produces sound welds
The base metal grade is correct
The radiographic technique is valid
A welder can deposit sound weld metal
content.explanation: The WPQ qualifies the welder's skill; the WPS/PQR qualify the procedure. Both are needed before production welding.

content.stem: A change in an ESSENTIAL variable on a qualified WPS requires:
options: Requalification of the WPS with a new PQR
Only a documented revision note on the WPS sheet
No corrective action of any kind is needed here
Issuing an entirely new stamped vessel nameplate
content.explanation: Essential variables affect mechanical properties; changing one beyond its qualified range requires requalifying the procedure. Nonessential variables require only WPS revision.

content.stem: Which of the following is an essential variable for a procedure qualification?
options: The WPS document revision number
A change in base-metal P-Number
The name of the testing laboratory
The fabricator's company logo
content.explanation: Base-metal P-Number grouping is an essential variable. Administrative items (rev number, lab name) are explicitly non-technical and excluded from exam scope.

content.stem: ASME Section IX P-Numbers are assigned to base metals primarily to:
options: Indicate the purchase price of the base metal
Specify a required surface color-coding scheme
Group base metals of similar weldability
Define the required pressure-relief set pressure
content.explanation: P-Numbers group base metals of similar characteristics (weldability) so that qualification on one member can cover others in the group, reducing required qualifications.

content.stem: F-Numbers in Section IX are used to group:
options: Base metals grouped by strength
NDE methods grouped by sensitivity
Heat treatments grouped by hold time
Filler metals grouped by usability
content.explanation: F-Numbers group filler metals/electrodes by their usability characteristics; A-Numbers address weld metal chemistry.

content.stem: For a typical groove-weld procedure qualification on plate, which mechanical tests are commonly required by Section IX?
options: Tension and guided-bend tests
Hardness testing of the HAZ only
Charpy impact testing only
Macro-etch examination only
content.explanation: Procedure qualification for groove welds typically requires tension tests and guided-bend tests (with impact tests added when supplementary essential variables/Charpy requirements apply).

content.stem: ASME Section V, Article 1 provides:
options: Acceptance criteria for every welded joint type
General requirements for use as a referenced code
Detailed radiographic technique procedure rules
Pressure-relief device inspection requirements
content.explanation: Article 1 covers general requirements: scope, responsibilities of Owner/User and subcontractors, calibration, and record-keeping for NDE.

content.stem: In radiographic examination (Section V, Article 2), the image quality indicator (IQI), or penetrameter, is used to:
options: Measure the remaining wall thickness directly
Detect only surface-breaking cracks that present
Verify the technique gives adequate sensitivity
Measure the base-metal surface hardness value
content.explanation: The IQI/penetrameter demonstrates that the radiograph has adequate sensitivity to reveal discontinuities of a given size; it does not directly measure flaw size.

content.stem: Radiographic film density requirements in Article 2 exist to ensure:
options: A lower purchase cost for the film stock used
A freshly painted surface applied over the weld
A grounded electrical bonding connection point
Reliable interpretation of the radiograph
content.explanation: Density limits ensure radiographs are neither too light nor too dark to interpret discontinuities reliably.

content.stem: Liquid penetrant examination (Section V, Article 6) is capable of detecting:
options: Discontinuities open to the surface
Subsurface laminations within the steel plate
Internal volumetric porosity beneath the surface
Remaining base-metal wall thickness values
content.explanation: PT detects only surface-breaking discontinuities; adequate dwell and proper developer application are essential.

content.stem: Adequate penetrant 'dwell time' is important because it:
options: The examined surface to first become fully clean
Penetrant to seep into surface openings
The applied developer layer to be wiped away
The relief valve set pressure to be established
content.explanation: Dwell time lets penetrant enter fine surface openings so they can later be revealed by the developer; too short a dwell can miss tight discontinuities.

content.stem: Magnetic particle examination using the yoke technique detects discontinuities that are:
options: Only deep flaws buried within the thick wall
Flaws in nonmagnetic stainless material only
Surface and near-surface in ferromagnetic metal
Discontinuities only after PWHT is fully complete
content.explanation: MT reveals surface and slightly subsurface discontinuities in ferromagnetic materials by leakage fields; it is not effective on nonmagnetic materials.

content.stem: Section V, Article 23 references SE-797 for:
options: Radiographic film density control requirements
Detailed liquid penetrant removal procedures
Pressure-relief valve bench testing methods
Manual ultrasonic pulse-echo thickness measurement
content.explanation: SE-797 is the standard practice for measuring thickness by manual ultrasonic pulse-echo contact — the method used for UT thickness gauging referenced in Article 23.

content.stem: When taking UT thickness readings, proper instrument calibration against a known reference is required to:
options: Ensure measurement accuracy for the material
Lower the overall cost of the examination work
Avoid the need for using any ultrasonic couplant
Remove the need for any qualified UT operator
content.explanation: Calibration on reference standards of known thickness/velocity for the material ensures accurate thickness measurement.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 201 addresses which repair method?
options: Mechanical bolted clamp pressure repair method
Butt-welded insert (flush patch) plates
Hot tapping of in-service live equipment lines
External protective surface coating application
content.explanation: Article 201 covers butt-welded insert plates (flush patches) installed by removing the damaged area and welding in a replacement section flush with the surface.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 211 covers weld buildup, weld overlay, and clad restoration. A weld overlay is typically used to:
options: Increase the overall diameter of the component
Reduce the rated MAWP value of the vessel
Restore lost wall or add a CRA layer
Replace the unit identification nameplate stamp
content.explanation: Weld buildup/overlay restores thickness or applies a corrosion-resistant layer; clad restoration re-establishes a damaged cladding.

content.stem: A fillet-welded patch plate (PCC-2 Article 212) is generally considered:
options: A flush insert repair equal to the base metal
A pressure-relief valve and device assembly
An applied external surface coating repair method
A lap patch evaluated for service limits
content.explanation: Fillet-welded (lap) patches are evaluated against service conditions and stress; they are not flush insert plates and have specific limitations.

content.stem: In-service welding onto pressure equipment (PCC-2 Article 210) introduces which primary concern that the procedure must control?
options: Burn-through and hydrogen cracking control
Maintaining overly excessive surface cleanliness
Preventing the loss of the equipment nameplate
Reducing the flow rate moving through the line
content.explanation: In-service welding must manage burn-through risk (thin remaining wall under pressure) and accelerated cooling that can cause hard, hydrogen-crack-prone microstructures.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 304 (flaw excavation and weld repair) requires that, after excavating a flaw, the cavity be:
options: Left in the original rough as-excavated condition
Verified flaw-free by PT or MT before repair
Filled with a sealant or compound type material
Coated over without any examination performed first
content.explanation: Excavated cavities are examined (typically PT or MT) to confirm complete flaw removal before and during weld repair.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 216 (welded hot taps) — a hot tap allows a new branch connection to be made:
options: Only after a complete shutdown and full draining
Without any welding being performed on it at all
On equipment kept in service under controls
Only on atmospheric storage tank vessel shells
content.explanation: Hot tapping installs a branch and cuts the opening while the equipment stays in service; it requires rigorous controls for burn-through, cooling, and ignition. Article 216 is in 510's PCC-2 scope but not 570's.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 312 specifically addresses inspection and repair of:
options: Aboveground storage tanks
Pressure-relief valve assemblies
Buried transmission piping
Shell-and-tube heat exchangers
content.explanation: Article 312 covers shell-and-tube heat exchanger inspection and repair; it is in 510's PCC-2 article list but not 570's.

content.stem: Original thickness 0.500 in. Ten years ago a reading was 0.430 in; the current reading (4 years later than that) is 0.400 in. What is the SHORT-TERM corrosion rate?
options: 0.01 in/yr
0.025 in/yr
0.003 in/yr
content.explanation: Short-term rate uses the two most recent readings: (0.430 - 0.400) / 4 = 0.0075 in/yr. The long-term rate over the full life is lower; API 510 lets the inspector use whichever governs.

content.stem: A component has t_actual = 0.360 in and t_required = 0.200 in. Long-term rate = 0.008 in/yr, short-term rate = 0.020 in/yr. What remaining life governs (the more conservative)?
options: 20 years
8 years
5.7 years
18 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required) / rate. Long-term gives 20 yr; short-term gives 8 yr. The shorter (more conservative) value, 8 years, governs the inspection planning.

content.stem: A vessel's remaining life is 7 years and no RBI assessment is used. What is the maximum internal or on-stream inspection interval?
options: 7 years
1.8 years
3.5 years
10 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (3.5 yr) or 10 years. Half-life governs: 3.5 years.

content.stem: A shell (inside radius 30 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0) measures 0.620 in. Corrosion rate is 0.015 in/yr and the next inspection is in 8 years. Using P = SEt/(R+0.6t), what MAWP applies for that interval (deduct future corrosion)?
options: 220 psi

content.stem: A Type 2 single-welded butt joint with a backing strip is fully radiographed. What joint efficiency applies per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: Type 2 (backing strip) with full RT is E = 0.90 in Table UW-12. Spot would be 0.80, none 0.65.

content.stem: A double full-fillet lap joint (Type 4) is used. What joint efficiency applies per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: A Type 4 double full-fillet lap joint is assigned E = 0.55 in Table UW-12 (no RT credit applies).

content.stem: When the longitudinal-stress (circumferential-joint) check governs an axial calculation, the required thickness is approximately what fraction of the circumferential-stress thickness?
options: About one-quarter
About equal
About one-half
About double
content.explanation: In a thin cylindrical shell the hoop (circumferential) stress is about twice the axial (longitudinal) stress. The longitudinal seam must resist the larger hoop stress, while the circumferential (girth) seam resists the smaller axial stress. So the thickness required by the circumferential-joint (axial) check is roughly half that required by the longitudinal-joint (hoop) check - which is why the longitudinal joint usually governs.

content.stem: A vessel part sits 70 ft below the liquid level (SG = 1.0). What static head pressure acts on it?
options: 15.2 psi
70 psi
60.6 psi
30.3 psi
content.explanation: Static head = 0.433 x height x SG = 0.433 x 70 x 1.0 = 30.31 psi.

content.stem: Find the required shell thickness (circumferential stress): P = 350 psi, R = 36 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 0.85. Use t = PR/(SE - 0.6P).
Find the required thickness of a 2:1 ellipsoidal head: P = 275 psi, inside diameter D = 48 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PD/(2SE - 0.2P).
Find the required thickness of a standard (6%) torispherical head: P = 300 psi, crown radius L = 48 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = 0.885PL/(SE - 0.1P).
content.explanation: t = (0.885 x 300 x 48)/((17500) - 0.1 x 300) = 12744/17470 = 0.7295 in. A torispherical head needs more thickness than a 2:1 ellipsoidal of the same diameter.

content.stem: A hemispherical head has t = 0.625 in, inside radius R = 40 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. What is its MAWP? Use P = 2SEt/(R + 0.2t).
A vessel has MAWP = 180 psi. The ratio of allowable stress at test temperature to design temperature is 1.15. What is the hydrostatic test pressure per UG-99(b)?
options: 234 psi
207 psi
content.explanation: Test pressure = 1.3 x MAWP x (S_test/S_design) = 1.3 x 180 x 1.15 = 269.1 psi.

content.stem: A fillet weld has a 0.625 in leg dimension. Using the 0.7 conversion factor, what is the effective throat?

For a radial nozzle in a cylindrical shell (correction factor F = 1.0), the required reinforcement area is A = d x tr x F. With finished opening d = 6.0 in and shell required thickness tr = 0.300 in, what is the required area?
options: 0.9 sq in
6.3 sq in
1.8 sq in
3.6 sq in
content.explanation: A = d x tr x F = 6.0 x 0.300 x 1.0 = 1.80 sq in. This is the area that must be replaced by available reinforcement within the limits of UG-40.

content.stem: A fillet-welded patch installed over a corroded area is generally considered which kind of repair?
options: A permanent repair that needs no later follow-up
An alteration that raises the rated vessel MAWP
A code-stamped new-construction pressure part
A temporary repair to be re-evaluated later
content.explanation: Lap/fillet-welded patches are typically treated as temporary repairs that must be tracked and re-evaluated, then made permanent or replaced as conditions warrant.

content.stem: A full-encirclement welded sleeve is most appropriate for restoring which condition?
options: A locally thinned or leaking shell course
A correctly sized pressure-relief device outlet
A vessel nameplate that has become illegible
An over-thick shell course that needs reduction
content.explanation: Full-encirclement sleeves restore pressure-containing capability over locally thinned, cracked, or leaking areas, distributing load around the circumference.

content.stem: After a welded repair requiring PWHT is completed, the inspector should ensure which step occurs?
options: The relief valve set pressure is afterward lowered
Appropriate NDE confirms acceptable weld quality
The vessel nameplate must be removed entirely first
The remaining corrosion allowance is set to zero
content.explanation: Repair welds are examined by appropriate NDE (often after PWHT) to verify the weld meets acceptance criteria before returning to service.

content.stem: The difference between vessel MAWP and a vessel-part MAWP is best explained by which factor?
options: The exterior paint color used on each section
The mounting location of the relief device tag
Static head adds to pressure at lower parts
The age of the original U-1 manufacturer report
content.explanation: A vessel-part MAWP accounts for static head at that elevation; the vessel MAWP is governed by the limiting part once static head is considered.

content.stem: Deferring a scheduled internal inspection beyond its due date generally requires which basis?
options: An informal verbal agreement among the operators
The vessel being fully repainted before the date
Removal of all the condition monitoring locations
A documented assessment justifying the deferral
content.explanation: Interval extensions/deferrals must be supported by a documented engineering or RBI assessment showing continued integrity; they are not informal decisions.

content.stem: Per API 510, the authorized inspector responsible for accepting inspection results must hold which?
options: A valid API 510 inspector certification
A welding performance qualification card
A radiographic film interpreter license
An operator process-control certificate
content.explanation: The authorized inspector must be certified to API 510; examiners performing NDE need not be API inspectors but work under the inspector's direction.

content.stem: Following a major alteration, a pressure test is normally required unless which alternative applies?
options: The operations team simply decides it is unnecessary
Suitable NDE is substituted with engineering approval
The vessel is now more than ten years old in service
The vessel nameplate is updated by re-stamping the data
content.explanation: After alterations a pressure test is the default; substitute NDE in lieu of testing may be allowed when justified and approved per the construction code and API 510.

content.stem: The number of CMLs on a vessel in non-localized, uniform corrosion service may be which?
options: Always greater than fifty monitoring points per vessel
Set only at the single relief device inlet nozzle
Fewer than for localized-corrosion service
Eliminated entirely because the corrosion is uniform
content.explanation: Uniform general corrosion can be monitored with relatively few representative CMLs; localized mechanisms require more CMLs placed to find the damage.

content.stem: The nameplate of a vessel that has been rerated should reflect which information?
options: Only the original construction data
The inspector's personal contact details
The coating manufacturer and batch
The new MAWP and the rerating date
content.explanation: After a rerating the nameplate (or an attached supplemental plate) is updated to show the new MAWP and the date, preserving traceability.

content.stem: To reduce brittle-fracture risk during a hydrotest, the metal temperature should be controlled how?
options: Kept warm enough for adequate toughness
Lowered as far below ambient as possible
Held exactly at the design temperature
Ignored because test water is cool
content.explanation: Hydrotesting at too low a metal temperature raises brittle-fracture risk; the test is performed with the metal warm enough to ensure adequate toughness (often a specified minimum above MDMT).

content.stem: Which surface condition most accelerates atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel?
options: A clean, dry, and well-painted exterior surface
Frequent wetting with poor drainage and salts
A continuously heated and completely dry surface
An inert-gas blanketed and fully sealed steel surface
content.explanation: Areas that stay damp, drain poorly, or collect salts corrode fastest; good coatings and drainage slow atmospheric corrosion.

content.stem: Which inspection finding is the strongest indicator of active CUI?
options: Dry insulation with a fully intact outer cladding
A freshly applied and painted external metal jacket
Wet or damaged insulation with rust staining
A correctly torqued nameplate retaining stud bolt
content.explanation: Wet, damaged, or stained insulation signals trapped moisture and likely CUI; intact dry insulation is a lower-concern indicator.

content.stem: Sulfidation rates of carbon steel are strongly influenced by which steel constituent?
options: Copper electroplating applied on the outer surface
Nickel content rising above roughly ten percent
Carbon content held below about one tenth percent
Silicon content of the carbon steel
content.explanation: Low-silicon carbon steels can corrode faster by sulfidation; silicon content materially affects the rate, which is why it is tracked in sulfidation circuits.

content.stem: A characteristic subsurface feature of advanced HTHA damage is which of the following?
options: Methane bubbles and fissuring at grain boundaries
Uniform external surface metal wastage throughout
A thick and protective magnetite scale layer formed
Chloride pitting across the inside wall surface area
content.explanation: HTHA produces internal decarburization and methane-filled fissures/cavities at grain boundaries, weakening the steel; it is screened with the API 941 Nelson curves.

content.stem: Amine stress corrosion cracking is most associated with which locations in an amine unit?
options: Fully stress-relieved austenitic stainless piping
Non-PWHT carbon steel welds in amine service
Cold low-stress water utility service piping lines
Externally insulated and dry blanketed process vessels
content.explanation: Amine SCC favors highly stressed (non-PWHT) carbon steel welds; PWHT is the principal mitigation.

content.stem: Which wet H2S mechanism specifically requires applied or residual tensile stress to propagate?
options: Hydrogen blistering forming at mid-wall laminations
Generalized atmospheric surface rusting of the steel
Sulfide stress cracking near hard weld zones
Uniform sulfidation occurring at elevated temperatures
content.explanation: SSC (and SOHIC) need tensile stress and are worse at hard microstructures; blistering/HIC can occur without applied stress.

content.stem: Erosion-corrosion damage is typically found at which piping/vessel features?
options: Long straight pipe runs carrying steady laminar flow
Externally insulated and capped dead-leg branches
Stagnant low-point drain pockets carrying little flow
Elbows and zones downstream of flow restrictions
content.explanation: High local velocity and turbulence at elbows, tees, and downstream of restrictions strip protective films and accelerate metal loss.

content.stem: Chloride SCC of austenitic stainless steel is promoted by which combination?
options: Chlorides, tensile stress, and elevated temperature
Pure clean water exposure at low ambient temperature
Sustained compressive surface stress in dry service
High nickel-alloy content under almost any condition
content.explanation: Cl-SCC needs chlorides, tensile stress, and (usually) elevated temperature; higher-nickel alloys are more resistant.

content.stem: Per UCS-56, the principal variable that sets the required PWHT holding time is which?
options: The color of the base material
The nominal thickness of the weld
The length of the vessel shell
The set pressure of the relief valve
content.explanation: PWHT holding time in UCS-56 is based on material P-Number group and nominal thickness, with minimum soak temperatures and times specified.

content.stem: The minimum design metal temperature (MDMT) of a vessel represents which of the following?
options: The measured hydrostatic test water temperature only
The maximum allowable vessel design temperature value
The lowest metal temperature for the coincident pressure
The ambient air temperature present during fabrication
content.explanation: MDMT is the lowest metal temperature (at the coincident pressure) for which the vessel is suitable; it drives impact-test requirements under UCS-66.

content.stem: Area-replacement reinforcement rules (UG-37) ensure which condition at an opening?
options: The opening is deliberately left without reinforcement
The nozzle is welded without any required inspection
The shell wall thickness is deliberately reduced locally
Metal removed for the opening is adequately replaced
content.explanation: Reinforcement rules require the strength of metal removed for the opening to be replaced within defined limits, maintaining pressure integrity.

content.stem: A category B circumferential head-to-shell joint is which type of welded connection?
options: A butt or corner joint per UW-13 details
A threaded mechanical screwed pipe connection
A bolted flange joint sealed with a ring gasket
A brazed lap connection used entirely on its own
content.explanation: Head-to-shell joints follow UW-13 welded-joint details (butt or acceptable corner joints), not threaded or bolted connections, for pressure integrity.

content.stem: A pneumatic test is sometimes used instead of a hydrostatic test primarily when which is true?
options: The operator simply prefers a much faster result
The vessel cannot safely hold test water
The vessel exterior is painted a very light color
The vessel identification nameplate was just replaced
content.explanation: Pneumatic testing (UG-100) is used where hydro is impractical (e.g., the vessel cannot tolerate the water weight or residual moisture), but it carries greater stored-energy hazard.

content.stem: A-Numbers in Section IX are used to classify which characteristic?
options: The relative price grade of the welding electrode
The painted color code marked on the filler metal
The chemistry of the deposited weld metal
The outside diameter of the connected base pipe wall
content.explanation: A-Numbers group ferrous weld-metal analysis (chemistry); F-Numbers group fillers by usability and P-Numbers group base metals.

content.stem: Changing a nonessential variable on a qualified WPS requires which action?
options: A complete requalification with new tests
Scrapping the existing PQR entirely
Re-stamping the vessel nameplate
Revising the WPS without requalification
content.explanation: Nonessential variable changes require only a WPS revision; essential variable changes require requalification (a new PQR).

content.stem: A welder qualified on pipe in the 6G position is generally qualified for which range?
options: All positions for the applicable diameters
Only the flat downhand welding position on plate
Only vertical-up fillet welds that are made on pipe
Only the exact 6G test coupon geometry as welded
content.explanation: The 6G (inclined fixed) position qualifies a welder for all positions within the applicable thickness and diameter ranges, which is why it is broadly used.

content.stem: Proper IQI (penetrameter) placement for radiography is normally on which side?
options: The film side of the part under all conditions
The source side of the part where practical
Away from the actual radiographic area of interest
On the penetrant developer tray work surface only
content.explanation: IQIs are placed source-side where practical (film-side placement is allowed with an 'F' marker and adjusted requirements) to verify radiographic sensitivity.

content.stem: Excess surface penetrant must be removed in a controlled way to avoid which outcome?
options: Adding extra penetrant into the developer layer
Heating the part well above its rated MDMT value
Washing penetrant out of real discontinuities
Lowering the overall vessel MAWP pressure rating
content.explanation: Over-aggressive removal can flush penetrant from genuine flaws, causing missed indications; removal is controlled per the procedure.

content.stem: Using two yoke leg orientations roughly perpendicular to each other addresses which limitation?
options: The magnetic particle yoke cannot be used on steel
The applied penetrant dwell time is far too short
The radiographic film density reading reads too high
Flaws aligned with the magnetic field go undetected
content.explanation: MT is most sensitive to flaws perpendicular to the field; examining in two perpendicular directions ensures flaws of any orientation are detected.

content.stem: A common cause of erroneous UT thickness readings on a corroded surface is which?
options: Rough or scaled back-wall scattering the echo
Using a correctly matched UT calibration block
Applying adequate couplant evenly across the surface
Calibrating the gauge on the same base material grade
content.explanation: Rough, pitted, or scaled surfaces scatter the ultrasonic echo and can cause false or missed readings; surface prep and proper calibration mitigate this.

content.stem: For detecting external CUI without full insulation removal, RP 572 notes the use of which?
options: Hardness testing of the vessel nameplate surface area
Profile radiography or other screening methods
Set-pressure bench testing of the relief valves only
Ferrite content measurement taken across the base metal
content.explanation: Screening methods such as profile/real-time radiography help find CUI without stripping all insulation; suspect areas are then exposed for direct inspection.

content.stem: When inspecting a vessel's nozzles, RP 572 highlights which area as prone to cracking?
options: The painted exterior surface area of the vessel head
The relief device discharge tailpipe outlet section
Nozzle-to-shell welds under cyclic loading
The clearly legible printed portion of the nameplate
content.explanation: Nozzle-to-shell junctions concentrate stress and can crack under thermal or mechanical cycling, warranting focused surface NDE.

content.stem: A relief valve found with a corroded, stuck disc most likely indicates which problem?
options: It will relieve well below set pressure
It improves the overall flow capacity
It needs no further bench testing
It may fail to open at the set pressure
content.explanation: Corrosion or fouling that sticks the disc can prevent the valve from opening at set pressure - a dangerous failure mode that bench testing is meant to catch.

content.stem: RP 576 recommends that relief device inlet and outlet piping be inspected for which condition?
options: Plugging or restriction that impairs relief
A fresh new coat of protective exterior surface paint
The correct identification nameplate stamping font size
An increased design corrosion allowance margin value
content.explanation: Inlet/outlet blockage or restriction can defeat a relief device even if the valve itself works; RP 576 stresses inspecting the connected piping.

content.stem: During welding inspection, verifying that the WPS essential variables were followed confirms which?
options: The vessel identification nameplate stays fully current
The production weld matches its qualified procedure
The pressure-relief valve was recently bench tested
The applied surface coating film thickness is adequate
content.explanation: Confirming the production weld stayed within the WPS essential-variable ranges is central to weld quality assurance under RP 577.

content.stem: Hydrogen-induced (delayed) cracking in carbon-steel welds is reduced primarily by which practice?
options: High-hydrogen welding rods used without any preheat
Rapid water quenching applied right after welding
Low-hydrogen consumables with adequate preheat
Skipping all electrode storage and drying oven controls
content.explanation: Low-hydrogen electrodes (properly stored) plus preheat reduce diffusible hydrogen and slow cooling, lowering delayed-cracking risk.

content.stem: Incomplete fusion in a weld is best described as which condition?
options: Excess weld reinforcement raised above the surface
Acceptable rounded and scattered porosity in the weld
A smooth and uniform weld cap top surface profile
Weld metal not fused to the base or prior pass
content.explanation: Incomplete fusion is a lack of coalescence between weld metal and the base metal or a previous pass; it is a planar defect that concentrates stress.

content.stem: A practical PMI method for verifying alloy in the field is which of the following?
options: Handheld X-ray fluorescence analysis of the metal
A simple visual color comparison of the surface paint
Weighing the whole component on a calibrated scale
Measuring the installed relief valve set pressure value
content.explanation: Portable XRF (and optical emission) analyzers identify alloying elements in the field, confirming the material matches the specification.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 209 (alternatives to PWHT) provides methods chiefly to achieve which goal?
options: Permission to skip all of the required weld inspection
Acceptable properties when PWHT is impractical
A method to raise the rated vessel MAWP rating value
A direct substitute for the pressure-relief device
content.explanation: Article 209 gives controlled-deposition and temper-bead alternatives that produce acceptable properties where conventional PWHT cannot be performed.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 305 addresses repair and conversion of which component?
options: Aboveground storage tank bottom floor plate sections
Pressure-relief valve internal trim and seat components
Damaged or mismatched bolted flange joints
Buried cathodic-protection sacrificial anode beds
content.explanation: Article 305 covers flange repair and conversion (e.g., refacing, seal-weld repair) of bolted flange joints.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 202 (external weld buildup to repair internal thinning) is appropriate when which holds?
options: The component has no remaining wall thickness at all
The installed pressure-relief device must be relocated
The vessel nameplate requires a complete re-stamping
Internal access is impractical but wall is thinned
content.explanation: External weld buildup restores wall where internal thinning exists and internal access is impractical, subject to remaining-wall and procedure controls. Article 202 is in 510's PCC-2 scope.

content.stem: A CML read 0.540 in five years ago and 0.475 in today. What is the corrosion rate?
options: 0.013 in/yr
0.026 in/yr
0.065 in/yr
0.095 in/yr
content.explanation: Rate = (t_previous - t_actual)/time = (0.540 - 0.475)/5 = 0.013 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.475 in, t_required = 0.250 in, corrosion rate = 0.013 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 8.7 years
17.3 years
36.5 years
19.2 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.475 - 0.250)/0.013 = 17.3 years.

content.stem: A vessel's remaining life is 16 years with no RBI assessment. Maximum internal inspection interval?
options: 16 years
4 years
8 years
10 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (8 yr) or 10 years. Half-life governs at 8 years.

content.stem: A component measures 0.512 in with a required thickness of 0.375 in. Remaining corrosion allowance?
content.explanation: Remaining corrosion allowance = t_actual - t_required = 0.512 - 0.375 = 0.137 in.

content.stem: A corroded shell: t = 0.450 in, inside radius R = 28 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. MAWP from P = SEt/(R + 0.6t)?
A hemispherical head: t = 0.300 in, inside radius R = 28 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. MAWP from P = 2SEt/(R + 0.2t)?
options: 375 psi

content.stem: Required shell thickness (circumferential stress): P = 425 psi, R = 30 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PR/(SE - 0.6P).
Required thickness of a 2:1 ellipsoidal head: P = 320 psi, inside diameter D = 54 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 0.85. Use t = PD/(2SE - 0.2P).
A Type 1 double-welded butt longitudinal joint is NOT radiographed. What joint efficiency applies per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: A Type 1 joint with no radiography is assigned E = 0.70 in Table UW-12 (full RT gives 1.00, spot RT 0.85).

content.stem: The MAWP at the top of a vertical vessel is 150 psi. A nozzle sits 40 ft below the top (SG = 1.0). What pressure (MAWP + static head) acts at the nozzle?
options: 150 psi
17.3 psi
content.explanation: Pressure = MAWP + static head = 150 + (0.433 x 40) = 167.3 psi.

content.stem: A vessel has MAWP = 240 psi and equal allowable stresses at test and design temperature. Standard hydrostatic test pressure per UG-99(b)?
options: 360 psi
240 psi
312 psi
264 psi
content.explanation: Test pressure = 1.3 x MAWP x (S_test/S_design) = 1.3 x 240 x 1.0 = 312 psi.

content.stem: A fillet weld requires a 0.28 in throat. Using the 0.7 factor, what leg dimension is needed?
options: 0.4 in

content.stem: For a radial nozzle (F = 1.0), required reinforcement area A = d x tr x F. With finished opening d = 8.0 in and shell required thickness tr = 0.250 in, what area must be replaced?
options: 2 sq in
1 sq in
8.25 sq in
4 sq in
content.explanation: A = d x tr x F = 8.0 x 0.250 x 1.0 = 2 sq in.

content.stem: A carbon steel vessel has a UCS-66 curve-derived MDMT of 10 F at its governing thickness. The owner wants to operate down to a minimum metal temperature of -5 F. Without further evaluation, what is required?
options: No further action because the vessel is already acceptable as currently built
Impact testing or another UCS-66/UG-20 basis to qualify the lower temperature
An automatic increase of the vessel rated MAWP at the new temperature point
Replacement of the pressure-relief device with a larger rated capacity one
content.explanation: The desired minimum temperature (-5 F) is below the established MDMT (10 F), so the vessel is not qualified there without additional basis - impact testing, an MDMT reduction per UCS-66.1, or a UG-20(f) exemption check.

content.stem: Under API 510, controlling the quality of repair and alteration work is whose responsibility?
options: The welder who deposits the repair metal
The jurisdiction inspecting once per decade
The owner/user managing the overall program
The coating crew applying the topcoat
content.explanation: The owner/user owns the program and its quality; the authorized inspector authorizes and accepts the work, and repair organizations execute it to qualified procedures.

content.stem: An examiner performing NDE under API 510 must meet which requirement?
options: Holding a current API 510 certification
Approval from the jurisdiction in writing
Ten years of operating experience first
Qualification to the applicable NDE procedure
content.explanation: Examiners must be qualified to the NDE method/procedure they perform; they need not be API-certified inspectors but work under the authorized inspector.

content.stem: The organization that performs a welded repair must work to which of the following?
options: Qualified procedures accepted by the inspector
Any convenient method the assigned welder prefers
Verbal instructions given by the operations team
A procedure written only after the work is done
content.explanation: Repairs follow qualified welding procedures acceptable to the authorized inspector; the work and its NDE are documented.

content.stem: An insulated vessel showing damaged insulation and possible CUI warrants which response?
options: No change to the existing inspection plan
Targeted inspection at the suspect locations
Immediate permanent retirement of the vessel
A reduction in the number of CMLs used
content.explanation: Evidence of CUI prompts targeted inspection (insulation removal or screening) at suspect areas; it does not justify ignoring the condition or cutting CMLs.

content.stem: API 579 fitness-for-service assessments are organized into tiered levels primarily to do what?
options: Set the total price charged for the analysis work
Define the welder performance qualification ranges
Match assessment rigor to the available data
Replace all of the routine inspection activity
content.explanation: API 579 uses Levels 1-3 of increasing rigor and data needs; lower levels are conservative screens, higher levels use more detailed analysis.

content.stem: A risk-based inspection program assesses risk as the combination of which two factors?
options: Vessel age combined with the original purchase cost
Paint surface condition and the nameplate clarity
Operator headcount and the assigned shift length
Probability of failure and consequence of failure
content.explanation: Risk = probability of failure x consequence of failure; RBI per API 580 uses both to prioritize inspection.

content.stem: Inspection records for a pressure vessel should be retained for which period?
options: The life of the vessel in service
Exactly one year after each inspection
Only until the next external inspection
Until the warranty period has ended
content.explanation: Permanent records (design, inspection history, repairs) are retained for the life of the vessel to support integrity decisions.

content.stem: Optimizing CMLs over time using inspection data and damage mechanisms means doing which?
options: Fixing them permanently at first install
Adjusting their number and location as needed
Removing them once any reading is taken
Placing them only on the nameplate boss
content.explanation: CML selection is refined over time - adding, relocating, or reducing points based on observed damage and the active mechanisms.

content.stem: When PWHT of a repair weld is impractical, an acceptable alternative may be which?
options: Skipping any form of stress management
Doubling the operating pressure briefly
Controlled-deposition or temper-bead welding
Leaving the weld fully un-inspected
content.explanation: Where PWHT is impractical, controlled-deposition/temper-bead methods (per the code and PCC-2 209) can produce acceptable properties.

content.stem: Discovering active leakage from a pressure vessel in service should prompt which first action?
options: Painting directly over the leaking area at once
Raising the vessel MAWP rating to try to stop it
Ignoring it entirely until the next turnaround
Assessing the hazard and planning a response
content.explanation: A leak is assessed for safety and cause; response (repair, derate, shutdown) follows. Painting or raising pressure is never the remedy.

content.stem: The most common mitigation for caustic SCC of carbon steel welds is which of the following?
options: Post-weld heat treatment of the weldments
Increasing the caustic concentration further
Operating at a higher metal temperature
Removing the corrosion allowance margin
content.explanation: PWHT relieves the weld residual stress that drives caustic SCC and is the usual mitigation for carbon steel; keeping service conditions below the susceptibility threshold also helps.

content.stem: Naphthenic acid corrosion severity is most influenced by which combination of factors?
options: Paint color, daylight, and nameplate size
Acid number, temperature, velocity, and alloy
Operator shift length and crew headcount
Relief set pressure and gasket material
content.explanation: NAC depends on total acid number (TAN), temperature (~425-750 F), velocity, and the alloy (molybdenum content improves resistance).

content.stem: The API 941 Nelson curves are used to do which of the following for HTHA?
options: Set the hydrostatic test pressure value for the vessel shell
Determine the relief valve discharge capacity that is needed
Screen steels against H2 partial pressure and temperature
Select the correct radiographic film density range to use
content.explanation: The Nelson curves plot safe operating limits of hydrogen partial pressure vs temperature for various Cr-Mo steels to screen HTHA susceptibility.

content.stem: Brittle fracture is most likely to initiate during which operating situation?
options: Steady operation at high temperature only
An idle vessel held under full vacuum
Normal flow at the design temperature
Pressurized startup at low metal temperature
content.explanation: Low metal temperature plus pressure (e.g., cold startup or hydrotest) combined with a flaw is the classic brittle-fracture scenario.

content.stem: A sudden increase in sulfidation rate at a piping circuit most likely points to which change?
options: Higher temperature or increased sulfur content
A fresh new coat of protective exterior surface paint
A newly updated equipment identification nameplate
A reduction in the assigned operator crew headcount
content.explanation: Sulfidation rises with temperature and sulfur level; an unexpected rate increase suggests a process change in one of those variables.

content.stem: Which coating strategy is a primary defense against CUI under insulation?
options: No coating at all so trapped moisture can evaporate
A suitable protective coating beneath the insulation
A much thicker layer of the same insulation material
A decorative finish paint on the outer metal jacket
content.explanation: A qualified protective coating under the insulation is a key CUI defense, along with sound weather barriers and moisture control.

content.stem: A practical way to reduce erosion-corrosion at a high-velocity elbow is which of the following?
options: Apply a thinner wall section to save on material
Increase the turbulence to clean the metal surface
Use a more resistant alloy or lower the velocity
Remove the elbow condition monitoring locations
content.explanation: Erosion-corrosion is reduced by lowering velocity/turbulence or upgrading to more erosion-resistant materials; thinning the wall worsens it.

content.stem: HCl corrosion in a crude overhead system is commonly mitigated by which practice?
options: Raising the overhead operating temperature setpoint
Removing the overhead condenser entirely from service
Increasing the chloride content carried in the feed
Caustic injection and effective desalting upstream
content.explanation: Desalting reduces chloride load and controlled caustic/neutralizer injection raises overhead pH, limiting HCl dew-point corrosion.

content.stem: ASME VIII-1 weld-joint details (UW-9 and related) primarily govern which aspect?
options: Joint design, alignment, and fit-up requirements
The purchase price of the welding consumables used
The color coding applied to the completed welds
The operator rest break schedule during a shift
content.explanation: These rules cover weld-joint design, edge preparation, alignment, and fit-up so the joint can be made and inspected reliably.

content.stem: Under UCS-56, the minimum PWHT holding temperature and time depend chiefly on which factor?
options: The exterior paint and jacket color
The P-Number group and the weld thickness
The vessel's installed elevation height
The relief valve's rated capacity
content.explanation: PWHT requirements in UCS-56 are tabulated by P-Number group and nominal thickness, with minimum soak temperatures and hold times.

content.stem: The reinforcement limits in UG-40 define which of the following for an opening?
options: The exact welding rod that must be used for it
The paint film thickness over the nozzle neck area
The zone within which replacement area counts
The torque value applied to the flange stud bolts
content.explanation: UG-40 sets the boundaries (parallel to the wall and normal to it) within which available reinforcement area may be credited for an opening.

content.stem: A key reason the hydrostatic test medium is usually water rather than gas is which?
options: Water automatically raises the vessel MAWP rating
Gas simply cannot be pressurized inside a vessel
Water entirely removes the need for any pressure test
Water stores far less energy if a failure occurs
